agenda_text:
This Agenda contains a brief general description of each item to be considered. Copies of the Staff reports or
  other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of
  the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. Any person who has a question concerning any of the
  agenda items may call the City Manager at (310) 603-0220, ext. 200.

  Procedures for Addressing the Council

  IN ORDER TO EXPEDITE CITY COUNCIL BUSINESS, WE ASK THAT ALL PERSONS WISHING TO ADDRESS THE
  COUNCIL SUBMIT YOUR COMMENTS IN ADVANCE TO CITYCLERK@LYNWOOD.CA.US OR FILL OUT A FORM
  PROVIDED AT THE PODIUM, AND TO TURN IT IN TO THE CITY CLERK PRIOR TO THE START OF THE
  MEETING. FAILURE TO FILL OUT SUCH A FORM WILL PROHIBIT YOU FROM ADDRESSING THE COUNCIL IN
  THE ABSENCE OF THE UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF THE COUNCIL.

  AGENDA
  City Council Regular Meeting
  TO BE HELD ON

  November 16, 2021

  COUNCIL CHAMBERS - 11350 BULLIS RD. LYNWOOD, CA 90262 or Web

  NON-AGENDA PUBLIC ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE COUNCIL ON ITEMS
  WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE
  AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL
  MAY REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A FUTURE MEETING.
  (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

  CONSENT CALENDAR
  ALL MATTERS LISTED UNDER THE CONSENT CALENDAR WILL BE ACTED UPON BY ONE MOTION
  AFFIRMING THE ACTION RECOMMENDED ON THE AGENDA. THERE WILL BE NO SEPARATE DISCUSSION ON
  THESE ITEMS PRIOR TO VOTING UNLESS MEMBERS OF THE COUNCIL OR STAFF REQUEST SPECIFIC
  ITEMS TO BE REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

  7.  APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated November 16, 2021 for FY 2021-2022. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant
  register dated November 16, 2021 for FY 2021-2022.

  8.  PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES
  Comments:
  Approving previous meeting minutes for Lynwood City Council (CC)
  June 1, 2021 City Council & Planning Commission Special Joint Meeting
  June 1, 2021 Regular Closed Session Meeting
  June 1, 2021 Regular City Council Meeting

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the Lynwood City Council approve the following minutes:
  June 1, 2021 City Council & Planning Commission Special Joint Meeting
  June 1, 2021 Regular Closed Session Meeting
  June 1, 2021 Regular City Council Meeting

  9.  CONTRACT APPROVAL FOR MUNISERVICES, LLC TO PROVIDE SALES AND
  USE, AND PROPERTY TAX ANALYSIS/AUDIT SERVICES
  Comments:
  The City contracts with MuniServices, LLC to provide sales and use, and property tax
  analysis/audit services. In addition, MuniServices assists the City in monitoring existing Measure
  PS and Measure RD Transaction and Use Tax revenues which commenced on April 1, 2017.
  The services provided by MuniServices, LLC enables the City to audit and forecast new
  transaction and use tax collections. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood adopt the attached resolution
  entitled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD
  AUTHORIZING THE APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH MUNISERVICES, LLC TO
  PROVIDE SALES AND USE, AND PROPERTY TAX ANALYSIS/AUDIT SERVICES”.

  10.  CONSIDERATION TO CANCEL AND DECLARE FUTURE CITY COUNCIL

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 2 of 198
   MEETINGS DARK
  Comments:
  Staff recommends that the City Council cancel and declare dark the Regular City Council
  Meetings of December 22, 2021 and August 16, 2022, and corresponding second meetings in
  August and December of forthcoming years. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council cancel and declare dark the Regular City Council
  Meetings on December 22, 2021 and August 16, 2022.

  11.  FOURTH AMENDMENT TO THE COMMUNICATIONS CONSULTING SERVICES
  AGREEMENT
  Comments:
  On October 20, 2020, the City Council approved a third amendment to the contract for the
  Kilkenny Group to provide communications consulting services and manage public relations
  matters for the City of Lynwood. These services are needed to promote City programs and
  events, manage media interactions, and provide related work as requested. The consultant is
  requesting to amend the agreement extending the term until June 30, 2022. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood adopt the attached resolution
  entitled; “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNW OOD, COUNTY
  OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA APPROVING A FOURTH AMENDMENT TO THE
  KILKENNY GROUP AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE COMMUNICATIONS CONSULTING
  SERVICES TO MANAGE BROADCAST MEDIA INTERACTIONS AND OTHER PUBLIC
  RELATIONS MATTERS FOR THE CITY OF LYNW OOD FROM JULY 1, 2021 UNTIL JUNE 30,
  2022, AT A MONTHLY COST NOT TO EXCEED $10,416."

  NEW/OLD BUSINESS
  12.  WRI AMENDED AND RESTATED FRANCHISE AGREEMENT, INCLUDING SB 1383
  COMPLIANCE/INDEMNIFICATION; PROP. 218 RATE IMPLEMENTATION W/3-YEAR
  SENIOR RATE FREEZE; 3-CART COLLECTION SYSTEM; AND A PROFESSIONAL
  PUBLIC OUTREACH CAMPAIGN
  Comments:
  Solid Waste Services have been a recent matter of consideration involving two separate, but
  related items: 1) Rate Adjustment; and 2) Update/Amendment of Contract Terms. Item number 1,
  Rate Adjustment, was t h e subjectof a majority protest hearing under Proposition
  218conducted during the regular City Council meeting of August 3, 2021. The proposed
  increases did not receive a majority protest and were subsequently approved by the City
  Council during the August 3rd meeting, on the condition that the maximum rate increase
  applicable to single family residential properties be reduced to an amount not to exceed $6.50
  (phased in over 3 years); and that the Senior Citizen Discounted R a t e s be
  frozen, with both conditions subject to Contractor’s concurrence.

  Tonight’s agenda item is to finalize number 2, Contract Terms, pursuant to the direction given by
  the City Council, and complete the process. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  That the City Council consider and approve the Amended and Restated Franchise Agreement
  between the City of Lynwood and Waste Resources, Inc. (WRI) as presented.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 3 of 198
   13.  AUTHORIZATION TO APPLY FOR SPECIFIED GRANT FUNDS
  Comments:
  With instrumental support from the Office of Assembly Speaker Anthony Rendon (District 63), the
  State of California’s Budget Act of 2021 made appropriations for the 2021–22 fiscal year that
  includes $1,500,000 for the City of Lynwood “…for community facilities, park, or recreational
  facilities construction, acquisition, or improvements.” In order to process the funding, a general
  authorizing resolution is required from the City’s governing body. (REC)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA APPROVING
  APPLICATION FOR SPECIFIED GRANT FUNDS.”

  14.  TERMINATION OF THE LOBBYING SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH LEGISLATIVE
  ADVOCACY GROUP
  Comments:
  On November 5, 2019, the City Council approved an agreement with Legislative Advocacy
  Group (LAG) to provide legislative services to the City on a month-to-month basis. This item is
  being presented per the request of one or more members of the City Council in order to seek
  direction and consent to provide LAG with a 30 day notice of intent to terminate LAG's
  agreement with the City. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council consider whether to provide LAG with a 30 day notice of
  intent to terminate LAG's agreement with the City or provide staff with alternative direction.

  15.  COUNCIL RECESS TO:
  Lynwood Housing Authority

  16.  CITY COUNCIL ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  17.  STAFF ORAL COMMENTS
  ADJOURNMENT
  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING WILL BE HELD ON DECEMBER 7, 2021 AT 6:00 P.M. IN THE
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS OF THE CITY HALL ANNEX, 11350 BULLIS ROAD, CITY OF
  LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA.

  DATE:  November 16, 2021

  TO:  Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council

  APPROVED BY: Ernie Hernandez, City Manager

  PREPARED BY: Michael M. Blazenski, Interim Director of Finance & Administration

  SUBJECT:  CONTRACT APPROVAL FOR MUNISERVICES, LLC TO PROVIDE SALES AND
  USE, AND PROPERTY TAX ANALYSIS/AUDIT SERVICES

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AUTHORIZING THE APPROVAL
  OF A CONTRACT WITH MUNISERVICES, LLC TO PROVIDE SALES AND USE, AND PROPERTY TAX
  ANALYSIS/AUDIT SERVICES”.

  Background:

  The City contracts with MuniServices, LLC to provide sales and use, and property tax analysis/audit services. In
  addition, MuniServices assists the City in monitoring existing Measure PS and Measure RD Transaction and
  Use Tax revenues which commenced on April 1, 2017. The services provided by MuniServices, LLC enables the
  City to audit and forecast new transaction and use tax collections.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  In October 2019, the City entered into a two-year agreement (October 6, 2019 through October 5, 2021) with
  MuniServices, LLC under the City Manager’s Purchasing Authority, for a not to exceed amount of $15,000. In
  September 2020, the agreement was amended for an additional $10,000 under the City Manager’s Purchasing
  Authority. In June 2021, Council authorized a second amendment to the agreement with MuniServices to increase
  compensation by $25,000 to cover costs for current and anticipated services to be paid prior to the end of the
  2020-21 fiscal year. The contract expired on October 5, 2021.

  The City of Lynwood has used the services of MuniServices, LLC since approximately 2010. In addition to
  providing sales and use, and property tax analysis/audit services, MuniServices, LLC has provided the City with
  statistical information annually for its comprehensive annual financial report. Staff is seeking Council’s approval to

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 33 of 198
   for a contract with MuniServices, LLC for a period of two years, for a not to exceed amount of $50,000.

  Lynwood Municipal Code Section 6-3.9 states that contracts over twenty-five thousand dollars in non-emergency
  situations are subject to a formal competitive bid process. However, Section 6-3.13 of the Lynwood Municipal
  Code authorizes the City Council to dispense with formal bidding requirements by a 4/5ths vote, when the services
  may be acquired more economically and efficiently through the use of an alternate procedure. Continuing services
  with MuniServices, LLC, will assist Finance & Administration with readily available information to perform analysis
  when reviewing and forecasting the City’s top revenue sources, property and sales tax.

  Fiscal Impact:

  Costs for service can be covered by the Finance & Administration Department’s FY 2021-22 operating budget.

   EXHIBIT A

  SCOPE OF WORK

  MuniServices, LLC understands that the City desires a vendor to conduct ongoing
  auditing, reporting, monitoring and analyses services of the City’s property tax, sales/use
  tax and utility users tax (specific to AB 1717) revenues. The City envisions the following
  services to be performed by MuniServices, LLC:

  1) Sales and Use Tax Audit

  a. Examine all sales and use tax records of the Board of Equalization
  pertaining to sales and use tax collected by the Board on behalf of the
  City.

  b. Perform ongoing sales tax audits in order to identify and correct point of
  sale distribution errors and thereby generate previously unrealized sales
  and use tax income for the City.

  c. Contact the appropriate management and accounting officials in
  companies that have businesses where a probability of error exists to
  verify whether current tax receipts accurately reflect the local sales
  activity. Such contacts will be conducted with the utmost courtesy and in
  a manner to encourage local business retention and expansion. Provide
  a report of all contacts and results thereof.

  d. Prepare and submit to the State Board of Equalization all information
  necessary to correct any allocation errors that are identified and follow-
  up with the individual businesses and the State Board of Equalization to
  ensure that all back quarterly payments due the City are recovered.

  e. If during the course of its audit, Contractor finds businesses located in
  the City that are properly reporting sales tax but have the potential for
  modifying their operation to provide an even greater share to the City,
  Contractor will work with those businesses and the City to encourage
  such changes.

  2) Sales/Use Tax Analysis & Reporting Service

  a. Provide quarterly analysis, customized newsletters, software, quarterly
  computer updates, and on-call assistance with sales tax projections for
  proposed projects. Work with the City’s economic development staff to
  track economic performance of City specified project areas, help identify
  voids and opportunities and provide data support and advice on alternate
  development strategies and business retention programs.

  1

  name, audit period start date, permit number, location allocation amount
  received by City and the amount due contractor. Provide applicable
  State Board of Equalization quarterly distribution report documents for
  the purpose of verifying and cross-referencing invoice amounts.

  c. Provide two-year sales and use tax forecast.

  SUBJECT:  WRI AMENDED AND RESTATED FRANCHISE AGREEMENT, INCLUDING SB 1383

  Recommendation:

  That the City Council consider and approve the Amended and Restated Franchise Agreement between the City
  of Lynwood and Waste Resources, Inc. (WRI) as presented.

  Background:

  The exclusive Solid Waste Handling Services Franchise with Waste Resources, Inc. (WRI), commenced on
  November 1, 2013, and was amended in 2017 to provide for the instatement of contractually authorized rates that
  had been disallowed up to that point, and to update the Agreement accordingly.

  In April of 2019, WRI requested consideration of a structural Rate Adjustment due to Extraordinary Cost Increases
  incurred to date, as well the transfer of the Residential Billing function to the LA County Tax Roll to offset the high
  cost of residential delinquencies that WRI estimated at fifty-plus percent (50+%) over sixty (60) days.

  By July of 2019, due to the complexities of the subject matter, the City had retained the professional services of
  MuniEnvironmental, LLC to assist with an in-depth financial review of WRI’s actual operating costs under the
  Lynwood Franchise.

  On December 17, 2019, MuniEnvironmental submitted a report of its findings from the Income and Expense
  Study it had conducted under its scope, stating that “WRI has suffered significant losses in the Residential and
  Industrial sectors during the entire term of the Agreement”; and, “Consultant find’s that City of Lynwood’s rates
  will need to be adjusted to meet current and pending program implementation costs, in addition to amending
  the current rate modification process to incorporate annual changes in disposal, operations and CPI. Lastly, the
  existing Franchise Agreement requires amending as the current Agreement is antiquated, lacking in current

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 67 of 198
   operational, collection and program methods”.

  Due to COVID-19 and related shutdowns, this dialog resumed in the second half of 2020.

  On November 17, 2020, the City Council approved the appropriation of funds to expand the scope of
  MuniEnvironmental’s Professional Services contract. The Staff Report recommended this appropriation, as
  follows: “…TO OBTAIN THE SERVICES OF MUNIENVIRONMENTAL TO PERFORM WORK ON THE
  RATE NEGOTIATIONS AND SOLID WASTE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT AMENDMENT AND
  IMPLEMENTATION OF A CITYWIDE ORGANICS RECYCLING”.

  During the same meeting, the City Council also authorized the then Acting City Manager to “…negotiate proposed
  rate increases for solid waste fees and contract terms…and return with a proposed amendment for the City
  Council’s future consideration”

  Discussion and Analysis:

  Solid Waste Services has been a recent matter of consideration involving two separate, but related items: 1) Rate
  Adjustment; and 2) Update/Amendment of Contract Terms. Item number 1, Rate Adjustment, was the subject of a
  majority protest hearing under Proposition 218 conducted during the regular City Council meeting of August 3,
  2021. The proposed increases did not receive a majority protest and were subsequently approved by the City
  Council during the August 3rd meeting, on the condition that the maximum rate increase applicable to single family
  residential properties be reduced to an amount not to exceed $6.50 (phased in over 3 years); and that the Senior
  Citizen Discounted Rates be frozen, with both conditions subject to Contractor’s concurrence.

  Tonight’s agenda item is to finalize number 2, Contract Terms, pursuant to the direction given by the City Council,
  and complete the process.
  California Senate Bill 1383 (SB 1383 – Organic Waste Recycling Law), is sweeping municipal solid waste and
  recycling legislation enacted to codify the California Air Resources Board's Short-Lived Climate Pollutant
  Reduction Strategy. It also drastically redefines and restructures the solid waste collection and recovery protocols
  in all local jurisdictions.
  Compliance with SB 1383 ultimately lies with the City. Under SB 1383, effective January 1, 2022, the City of
  Lynwood, along with all other Cities in California, must collect organic and food waste generated at all properties
  (residential, commercial and industrial) and recover at least 50% of such materials or face compliance violations
  and potential penalties and fines. SB 1383 also mandates new programs, while the standard for recovery steps up
  to seventy-five percent (75%) on January 1, 2025.
  In the restated franchise agreement, the City has placed the burden for compliance with SB 1383 on the franchise
  holder, thereby requiring an amended and restated agreement with different terms that are consistent with
  CalRecycle guidelines. MuniEnvironmental has accounted for the many regulatory requirements under SB 1383,
  by creating new service and performance standards that WRI must meet from this point forward or fall into material
  breach. In addition, CalRecycle’s SB 1383 implementation guidance is for jurisdictions to “…consider the
  relationship of the effective date and term of their franchise agreement and their need to comply with the
  majority of SB 1383 Regulatory requirements no later than January 1, 2022, and additional SB 1383
  Regulatory requirements by January 1, 2024.”
  Therefore, the franchise term has been amended to allow for the recovery of significant capital investment and to
  keep pace with heightened recovery standards in the future.
  A case-in-point is the conversion to a 3-Cart Collection System for all residential cart customer in the City. This
  costly service upgrade is now a core component pursuant to SB 1383 Regulations (14 CCR, Division 7, Chapter
  12, Article 3), defining it as the Three (3) Plus Container Collection System (Blue, Green, And Gray Cart),
  including a Food Waste Caddy (the “Plus” designation refers to the Food Waste Caddy), and is foundational to
  the Standard Compliance Approach.
  In keeping with these new regulatory requirements, as well as all other outstanding issues addressed during
  negotiations with WRI, the Amended and Restated Franchise Agreement contains material changes in the
  franchise agreement provisions as identified below:
  Guaranteed Compliance with SB 1383, with Indemnification to the City (including other related laws);
  Residential Three (3) Plus Cart Plus Collection System as defined under SB 1383 Regulations:

  o Food Waste Kitchen Caddies furnished to all residential customers;

  o New Clean-Fuel Collection Vehicles to provide third cart;

  coverage of the AB 341 Commercial Recycling Program;
  Inspection/Enforcement Protocols performed by WRI for City, w/Site Inspections;

  This Second Amended and Restated Agreement for Exclusive Solid Waste Handling Services
  (“Agreement”), by and between the City of Lynwood, a municipal corporation of the State of California
  (“City”), and Waste Resources, 1nc., a California corporation organized under the laws of the State of
  California (“Contractor”), is made and entered into this 1st day of October, 2021.

  RECITALS

  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Public Resources Code Section 40059(a)(2) and the
  Lynwood Municipal Code, Chapter 9, §9.1.6, the City Council of the City of Lynwood has determined
  that the public health, safety, and well-being require that an Exclusive Franchise Agreement for Solid
  Waste Handling Services for Single Family, Multi-Family, and Commercial/Industrial Customers be
  awarded to a qualified company for the Collection and subsequent Transfer, Transportation, Recycling,
  Processing, and/or Disposal of Municipal Solid Waste Materials generated within the City; and,

  WHEREAS, City and Contractor (collectively, the “Parties”) entered into that certain Agreement
  between City and Contractor for Solid Waste Handling Services, effective November 1, 2013 (“Original
  Agreement”), wherein WRI was granted an exclusive franchise to provide solid waste handling services
  within the City; and,

  WHEREAS, City and Contractor entered into the “First Amended Solid Waste Handling
  Services Agreement”, dated the 15th of November, 2017 (“First Amended Agreement”), modifying
  portions of the Original Agreement; and,

  WHEREAS, the Original Agreement and the First Amended Agreement shall be collectively
  referred to as the “Previous Agreements”; and, now the Parties desire to amend, restate, update, and
  supersede the Previous Agreements to accurately reflect the rights and obligations of the City and
  Contractor solely as forth in this Agreement; and,

  WHEREAS, the Legislature of the State of California, by enactment of the California 1ntegrated
  Waste Management Act of 1989 (AB 939/California Public Resources Code Section 40000, et seq.), has
  declared that it is in the public interest to authorize and require local agencies to make adequate provisions
  for Solid Waste handling within their jurisdictions; and,

  WHEREAS, the State of California has found and declared that the amount of Solid Waste
  generated in California, coupled with diminishing Disposal capacity and interest in minimizing potential
  environmental impacts from landfilling and the need to conserve natural resources, have created an urgent
  need for State and local agencies to enact and implement an aggressive integrated waste management
  program. The State has, through enactment of AB 939 and subsequent related legislation including, but

  Bulky Items Collected pursuant to this Agreement may not be landfilled until the following
  hierarchy of diversion efforts has been observed by Contractor:

  (B)  Disassemble for reuse or Recycling;

  (C)  Recycle, Transformation, other means of diversion; and,

  (D)  Disposal.

  This hierarchy is intended to preclude the use of front or rear loading packer vehicles for
  Bulky Items unless the compaction mechanism is not used to compact the Bulky Items. The
  disposition of Bulky Items shall be tracked by Contractor and this information shall be included in
  Contractor's quarterly reports to City.

  10.2.1 General

  Contractor acknowledges and agrees that Public Education and Outreach are critical, key,
  and essential elements of any efforts to achieve the fundamental requirements of AB 939.
  Accordingly, Contractor agrees to exploit opportunities to expand public and Customer knowledge
  concerning needs and methods to reduce, reuse and recycle Solid Waste and to cooperate fully

  Contractor shall maintain its own program of providing information, in the form of billing
  inserts and Website content, relevant to Solid Waste Handling Services and related issues, such as
  reminders of services available, call center hours, and/or other Contractor/City related information
  that might enhance and improve Customers’ overall service experience. All public education
  materials shall be approved in advance by City, and produced in English and Spanish. Additional
  languages may be required during the Term of this Agreement.

  10.2.2 Program Objectives

  Contractor’s Public Education and Outreach strategy shall focus on improving Generators’
  understanding of the benefits and opportunities that exist with Source Reduction, Reuse, and
  Landfill Disposal avoidance. In general, Contractor-provided Public Education and Outreach,
  which shall include all content required by this Section 10.2, should: (i) inform Generators about
  the services that are provided under this Agreement with specific focus on describing the methods
  and benefits of Source Reduction, Reuse, and avoidance of Solid Waste Disposal; (ii) instruct
  Generators on the proper method for placing materials in Containers for Collection and setting
  Containers out for Collection with a specific focus on minimizing contamination of Source
  Separated Recyclable Materials and Source Separated Green Container Organic Waste
  (SSGCOW); (iii) clearly define Excluded Waste and educate Generators about the hazards of such
  materials and their opportunities for proper handling; (iv) discourage Generators from buying

  advisory ruling on Contractor's allegations, and suggest a remedy if a breach by City is determined to

  SUBJECT:  AUTHORIZATION TO APPLY FOR SPECIFIED GRANT FUNDS

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA APPROVING APPLICATION FOR SPECIFIED
  GRANT FUNDS.”

  Background:

  With instrumental support from the Office of Assembly Speaker Anthony Rendon (District 63), the State of
  California’s Budget Act of 2021 made appropriations for the 2021–22 fiscal year that includes $1,500,000 for the
  City of Lynwood “…for community facilities, park, or recreational facilities construction, acquisition, or
  improvements. ” In order to process the funding, a general authorizing resolution is required from the City’s
  governing body.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  The State of California’s Budget Act of 2021 made appropriations for the support of state government for the
  2021–22 fiscal year. The “Parks, Recreation, and Resources” subsection of SEC. 273. - Section 19.56 was
  added to the Budget Act of 2021 (Assembly Bill 128 of 2021), to read:

  SB-129 Budget Act of 2021. (2021-2022)

  SEC. 273. Section 19.56 is added to the Budget Act of 2021 (Assembly Bill 128 of 2021), to read:

  SEC. 19.56. (a) (1) The amounts appropriated pursuant to this section reflect legislative priorities.

  (2) Unless otherwise specified, the funds appropriated in this section shall not be disbursed for any
  project prior to September 30, 2021. Future legislation may, but is not required to, specify further details

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 192 of 198
   concerning the manner of disbursement of these funds.

  (b) The amounts specified in this subdivision are hereby appropriated from the General Fund as
  follows..:

  (87) $1,500,000 to the City of Lynwood for community facilities, park, or recreational facilities
  construction, acquisition, or improvements.
  On Tuesday, October 26, 2021, staff met with Lynwood’s Project Officer from the CA Department of Parks &
  Recreation - Office of Grants & Local Services (OGALS), the office that will manage the appropriation. The
  Project Officer informed staff that:

  1. These appropriations will be managed as “specified grants” that will closely follow Prop. 68-type grant
  guidelines.
  2. A Procedural Guide is in development by OGALS.
  3. A general authorizing resolution is required before 12/31/21, as presented.

  The Authorizing Resolution presented and recommended for approval serves two general purposes:

  1. It is the official means by which the grantee Governing Body agrees to the terms of the grant agreements.
  2. Designates a position title (Lynwood City Manager) to represent the Governing Body on all matters
  regarding projects associated with the grant agreements.

  The appropriation funding is restricted to use for “…community facilities, park, or recreational facilities
  construction, acquisition, or improvements.” Staff is developing a formal project recommendation, but it is
  anticipated that the funds will ultimately support a significant renovation of the 67-year old Natatorium facility. Staff
  recommends that the City Council adopt the authorizing resolution as presented in this staff report.

  Fiscal Impact:

  The action requested within this staff report does not have a fiscal impact.
